sources.entry: parsy - Easy, generic parser combinator library for creating parsers.

summary.one_liner: Parsy is a small, dependency-free Python parser combinator library for building text parsers by composing simple parsers into larger ones.
summary.what_it_does: Parsy lets you write parsers by combining small parser objects into larger ones, in the style of Parsec, Parsnip and Parsimmon, as described in the README. The README points to a SQL SELECT statement example and a JSON parser as examples of the declarative code style. It is implemented in a single module of under 800 lines of code, which the README says could be vendored directly. The library has zero dependencies beyond the standard library. The README says it is essentially complete and no rewrites are planned, though compatible improvements are still considered. Documentation, a changelog and a PyPI package are linked from the README.
use_cases: build a parser for a custom text format
parse SQL SELECT statements in Python
write a JSON parser from small combinators
parse structured log or config text
vendor a small parsing library into a project
replace regex-based text parsing with composable grammars
notable: Zero dependencies outside the Python standard library
Implemented in a single module under 800 lines, easy to vendor
Monadic parser combinator style for LL(infinity) grammars
Stated as mature and stable, with few backwards incompatibilities over 10 years
caveats: The README states the project is essentially complete with no rewrites planned, so new features are unlikely beyond compatible improvements
Designed for LL(infinity) grammars, so it is a poor fit for grammars that need other parsing strategies (the README does not discuss this further)
